prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original game-ready SFC-style detailed pixel fish sprites, crisp stepped contours, square pixels, natural silver scale highlights, not a photo. TRUE TRANSPARENT ALPHA background; no shadow, vignette, ground, scenery, text, numbering or checkerboard. 1536x1024 atlas. Exactly SIX rows by FIVE columns, all cells same size. Row1 FIVE fish, row2 FIVE fish, row3 FIVE fish, row4 FIVE fish, row5 FIVE fish, row6 ONE fish in first cell and four EMPTY cells: TOTAL26 FISH, not21. Transparent 12px gutters and every fish intact within its own cell. One species only: UGUI Japanese dace Tribolodon hakonensis. Long streamlined spindle body, normal adult NONBREEDING colors, dark olive-gray back, silver flanks with one narrow dark charcoal lengthwise stripe, white belly, subtle ochre-orange soft pelvic/anal fins, deeply forked tail, tiny terminal mouth and modest round snout, normal round dark eye. It is a cyprinid dace and anatomically has exactly ONE small triangular soft dorsal fin near MIDBACK. All back between this one dorsal fin and the tail is totally SMOOTH: ABSOLUTELY NO ADIPOSE FIN, NO SECOND DORSAL FIN, NO tiny bump, no little triangle or dot on the back near tail. No barbels, no trout spots or parr marks, no big carp belly. Body excluding fins about4.5 times longer than tall. Slots0-24 follow gradual horizontal yaw every7.5degrees: slot0 full RIGHT profile, slot12 exactly FRONT, slot24 full LEFT profile. Same individual, fins, body proportions and stripe throughout; no roll or tilt. Front view narrow foreshortened body, both eyes and paired pectorals, no distorted fat face. Slot25=right full profile with slightly OPEN mouth. Centered at consistent scale in all26 cells. Exactly25 closed-mouth yaw poses plus1 open-mouth profile. This correct clean atlas will be cropped directly in game, so keep grid regular and draw ALL25 turn poses.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original sprite atlas for a Japanese SFC-style fishing game. Crisp detailed PIXEL ART, small square pixels, stepped outlines, limited harmonious natural palette, fine scales and fin rays, no smooth painting or photographic texture. REAL TRANSPARENT ALPHA background. Landscape canvas 1536 x 1024. Exactly 5 columns x 6 rows. 26 complete fish, slots 0-25 in row-major order, other four slots of last row empty. Cell spacing regular and 14 transparent pixels around each intact silhouette. Same individual and anatomy in every slot. Slots 0-24: slow horizontal YAW turn every 7.5 degrees, slot0 full RIGHT facing profile, slot12 exactly FRONT facing, slot24 full LEFT facing profile. No roll, no tilt, no vertical bend, no body deformation or fin removal. Front view has a narrow foreshortened body with both eyes and paired pectorals. Slot25 is full RIGHT profile with mouth slightly OPEN for breathing. Uniform center and scale; tail and every fin must fit within its cell. No grid lines, labels, numbers, text, hook, shadow, backdrop, water or checkerboard. Species anatomy must be accurate and stable across turn frames. No adipose fin unless explicitly requested. OIKAWA Opsariichthys platypus, mature Japanese male with vivid breeding colors. Streamlined shallow river fish, body excluding fins about 4 times longer than tall, small slightly upturned mouth. Olive green back, shimmering blue-green silver sides carrying about 8 narrow irregular rose-pink VERTICAL bands, white lower belly, turquoise/rose pectoral/pelvic fins. One low triangular dorsal fin near middle and a distinctly LONG softly triangular ANAL fin trailing backwards below rear body (important identifying male anatomy), deeply forked reddish gray tail, narrow peduncle. Do not draw an adipose fin or salmon shape. Colors and vertical bands remain attached and coherent in all turn poses. Front view must retain fish proportions and fine pectorals, not huge toy eyes.

KAWAHAGI Japanese thread-sail filefish Stephanolepis cirrhifer. Laterally compressed tall diamond-shaped body, olive tan and ochre mottled skin with irregular subtle dark brown cloud patches. Tiny protruding puckered terminal mouth at front of pointed snout, dark eye high on head; rough leather skin, NOT large carp scales. A single erect thin FIRST DORSAL SPINE above head, separate low soft SECOND dorsal fin on rear half of back, low long anal fin opposite it below rear body; small transparent pectoral fin; narrow caudal peduncle with fan-like rounded edged tail. No pelvic fan fins, no continuous bream dorsal fin, no adipose fin. A little threadlike leading ray on second dorsal may be visible in side profiles. Tall diamond silhouette is the key identity. In front view body becomes slender edge-on but head and eye pair remain anatomically real. Keep the little pouting mouth identifiable through every yaw and opening pose.
